decisions.reason: After several years with no visible continued promotion, this core cardboard display likely failed to clear aspiration levels strongly enough to justify keeping capacity tied up, so management would reallocate resources to better-performing standard offers or new development.

Although close to existing capabilities, the pegboard-backed variant appears not to have generated enough sustained demand or differentiation relative to aspirations, making withdrawal the more likely choice in a focused portfolio review.

This quarter-pallet cardboard display fits the core range, but by 2022 the absence of market visibility suggests learning has largely run its course and resources are better shifted to stronger products and newer projects.

Because the eighth-pallet format serves a narrower use case and has not remained visibly marketed, it is especially likely to be judged below aspiration and dropped in favor of more broadly successful display formats.

The wooden display pallet is less central to the firm's main cardboard-based routines and, without evidence of sustained success, behavioral-theory logic points to withdrawal and redeployment of resources to the established core and fresh innovation.
